body:
`#235` and then `#262` fixed the **Python** base parser so a backtick span wins only when it
*starts* the field. The **bash twin** that `C4-verify` uses — `_brief_base()` in the
template-shipped `engine/scripts/run-verify.sh` — still carries the pre-#235 rule, so the two
implementations of one parse now disagree.

## Demonstrated divergence (on #235's own example)

Brief field:

```
- **Repo + branch target:** getwyrd/wyrd @ main (feature branch `feat/x-slice`)
```

```console
$ python3 -c "from pdca_harness.publish import _clean_ref; print(_clean_ref(' main (feature branch \`feat/x-slice\`)'))"
main
$ PDCA_BUNDLE=/tmp/b_paren engine/scripts/run-verify.sh --print-base
origin/feat/x-slice
```

Publish opens the PR against `main`; `C4-verify` validates against `feat/x-slice`.

## The code

```python
# src/pdca_harness/publish.py:400-414 — fixed by #235/#262
m = re.match(r"`([^`]+)`", raw)      # ANCHORED: only a span at the START wins
token = m.group(1) if m else (raw.split()[0] if raw.split() else "")
```

```bash
# engine/scripts/run-verify.sh:166-178 — still the old rule
if [[ "$raw" == *'`'*'`'* ]]; then   # UNANCHORED: any span, anywhere after the @
  tok="${raw#*\`}"; tok="${tok%%\`*}"
```

## Why it survived two closures

`engine/tests/test_run_verify.sh:140-145` **pins the buggy behaviour**, and does so in the name
of parity:

```bash
# the _clean_ref quirk publish uses: a backticked branch in trailing prose wins over the
# plain token — run-verify MUST match publish so both cut from the SAME base.
check "backtick span wins (matches publish._clean_ref) -> origin/feat/x-slice" \
  "origin/feat/x-slice" ...
```

That comment was true before #235. After it, the test enforces the divergence it exists to
prevent — which is why #235 (closed 2026-07-04) and #262 (closed 2026-07-09) both left this
side untouched.

## Impact

`_resolve_base_ref` prefixes the result with the remote, so a hijacked token usually yields a
ref that does not exist (`origin/origin/main` for a field carrying an `origin/...` span in
prose) → warn + fall back to `origin/main`. For a bundle whose real base is **not** `main` — a
stacked slice targeting an integration branch, or a dependency-wave bundle — the fallback base
is wrong, and `C4-verify` then either false-fails with *"patch does not apply — the bundle is
stale"* or proves red→green against a tree that lacks the prereq. That is the exact damage
recorded for #454 and re-filed as #262.

Concretely (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca, `results/issue_649`, 2026-08-01): a brief base written
``getwyrd/wyrd @ main   (verified at Plan: `origin/main` = `9120f7a` …)`` resolves to
`origin/origin/main` in bash and `main` in Python. Masked there only because a wave>0 bundle is
handed `$PDCA_VERIFY_BASE`, which takes precedence — it bites a standalone `pdca gates <id>` and
any ordinary single-bundle brief that puts a backtick anywhere after the `@`. The planner had to
work around it by stripping backticks from the field, which is not a rule any brief author
should have to know.

## Fix

1. Mirror `_clean_ref` in `_brief_base()`: honour a backtick span **only** when it is the first
   non-space content after the `@`; otherwise take the first whitespace token. Both directions —
   parenthetical aside *and* trailing prose.
2. Update `engine/tests/test_run_verify.sh:140-145` to assert the anchored result (`origin/main`
   for the example above) and keep a case for a legitimately backticked base
   (`@ \`feat/x\`` → `origin/feat/x`), so parity is pinned to the *current* `_clean_ref`.
3. Worth considering so this cannot recur a fourth time: have the shell hook call the Python
   parser (both are already reachable in a rendered instance), or generate the shell case table
   from `_clean_ref`'s tests — one bug in two languages is what produced #235 → #262 → this.

The `--print-base` test hook already exists, so all of this is cheap to pin.

Refs #235, #262, #454, #91.
title: run-verify.sh _brief_base still takes a backtick span anywhere after @ — bash twin never got the #235/#262 anchoring fix
